children.title: Trump Orders U.S. Withdrawal from the World Health Organization
children.description_short: A Jan. 20, 2025 order directs steps toward U.S. withdrawal from WHO; it does not say membership ended that day.
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order stating that the United States intended to withdraw from the World Health Organization. It directed officials to pause future U.S. transfers, recall and reassign personnel, identify partners for necessary WHO activities, and cease negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement while withdrawal was in progress. The order does not establish that membership ended on January 20.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order stating that the United States intended to withdraw from the World Health Organization. It directed the Secretary of State and Office of Management and Budget to pause future U.S. funds, support and resources to WHO; recall and reassign government personnel or contractors working with the organization; and identify U.S. and international partners to assume necessary WHO activities. The order also directed the Secretary of State to cease negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement and amendments to the International Health Regulations while withdrawal was in progress. This is an order to pursue withdrawal, not proof that the United States left WHO on January 20. The frozen entry incorrectly said the country withdrew from both WHO and UNESCO that day; the UNESCO action is a separate later claim and is kept in a second internal draft. The order's text does not establish the broader outcome claims in the frozen synopsis, so this card does not state that U.S. departure had already removed the country from disease-surveillance networks or produced quantified public-health harms.

source_fact_map.fact: The Jan. 20 order states that the United States intends to withdraw from WHO.
source_fact_map.quote: The United States intends to withdraw from the WHO.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The White House January 20, 2025. WITHDRAWING THE UNITED STATES FROM THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION. Sec. 2. Actions. (a) The United States intends to withdraw from the WHO. The Presidential Letter to the Secretary-General of the United Nations signed on January 20, 2021, that retracted the United States’ July 6, 2020, notification of withdrawal is revoked.

source_fact_map.fact: The order directs officials to pause future transfers and reassign personnel or contractors working with WHO.
source_fact_map.quote: pause the future transfer of any United States Government funds, support, or resources to the WHO
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The Secretary of State and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall take appropriate measures, with all practicable speed, to: (i) pause the future transfer of any United States Government funds, support, or resources to the WHO; (ii) recall and reassign United States Government personnel or contractors working in any capacity with the WHO; and (iii) identify credible and transparent United States and international partners to assume necessary activities previously undertaken by the WHO.

source_fact_map.fact: The order directs the Secretary of State to cease negotiations while withdrawal is in progress.
source_fact_map.quote: While withdrawal is in progress, the Secretary of State will cease negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement and the amendments to the International Health Regulations
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Sec. 4. Global System Negotiations. While withdrawal is in progress, the Secretary of State will cease negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement and the amendments to the International Health Regulations, and actions taken to effectuate such agreement and amendments will have no binding force on the United States.

children.title: U.S. UNESCO Withdrawal Decision Reported for July 2025 (Unverified)
children.description_short: Prior research says the U.S. chose to leave UNESCO in July 2025, with departure set for December 2026; the cited page could not be checked.
children.description_medium: According to the supplied packet, UNESCO Director-General Audrey Azoulay announced a U.S. decision to withdraw on July 22, 2025, effective at the end of December 2026. The cited UNESCO page returned an automated human-verification screen and could not be checked. A February 4 White House order required a review of UNESCO membership, not an immediate withdrawal; the July claim remains unverified and this draft is not publication-eligible.
children.description_long: The supplied research packet attributes a July 22, 2025 announcement to UNESCO Director-General Audrey Azoulay and says the United States had decided to withdraw from UNESCO, with departure to take effect at the end of December 2026. Those supplied details correct the frozen entry's January 20 date and distinguish a future withdrawal from a completed exit. The cited UNESCO statement could not be inspected during this review: a direct request returned an automated human-verification screen, while the connected Exa service returned an authorization error and Firecrawl reported that its credits were exhausted. The White House's February 4 order, which was fetched directly, says only that the United States would review its UNESCO membership within 90 days; it does not establish a July withdrawal decision or an enacted departure. This internal draft therefore preserves the supplied chronology for review, labels the central announcement and effective date unverified, and does not state that the United States has already left UNESCO. The original January 20 date is not supported for this UNESCO claim. Publication requires an accessible source excerpt confirming the announcement and timing.

This review shall be led by the Secretary, in coordination with the United States Representative to the United Nations (UN Ambassador), and must be completed within 90 days of the date of this order.

terminal_record.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an order stating that the United States intended to withdraw from the World Health Organization and directing prospective funding and personnel changes. The supplied materials describe a separate UNESCO withdrawal announcement on July 22, with withdrawal expected at the end of December 2026, while a February 4 order called for a review. The UNESCO statement could not be read, so those details remain unverified. The frozen record combines different dates and actions.
terminal_record.description_long:
On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order stating that the United States intended to withdraw from the World Health Organization. The order directed officials to pause future U.S. funding and support, recall or reassign personnel and contractors working with WHO, identify partners for necessary activities, and stop negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement and amendments to the International Health Regulations while withdrawal was in progress. The order does not say that U.S. membership ended that day, and this draft makes no claim about resulting health effects.

The frozen record also says the United States withdrew from UNESCO on January 20. The supplied research materials instead place a separate UNESCO withdrawal announcement on July 22, 2025, with an effective date at the end of December 2026, and describe the February 4, 2025 executive order as directing a review of U.S. support to international organizations. Those UNESCO details remain unverified here: the cited page returned a human-verification screen, and the supplied account does not independently prove the announcement or effective date. This internal draft separates the events and marks the UNESCO claim as unverified. The parent remains ineligible for publication.
